newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: FORECAST-Poll cuts Singapore 96 growth to +6.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Poll cuts Singapore 96 growth to +6.5 pct.

text.p: Economists have cut their forecasts for growth of the Singapore economy this year by 0.6 percentage points to 6.5 percent year-on-year, a Reuters poll of leading financial institutions showed on Friday.
The poll of 12 economists, carried out on Thursday and Friday, also lowered slightly the average forecast for growth in 1997 to 7.0 percent year-on-year, from 7.2 percent.
Reuters' previous poll of forecasts for Singapore's growth was published on September 11.
Singapore's gross domestic product (GDP) grew by 8.8 percent in 1995 and 10.2 percent in 1994.
The latest poll produced an average forecast for Singapore's GDP growth in the third quarter of 3.5 percent year-on-year. The previous poll had predicted third quarter growth at 4.9 percent.
Growth in the fourth quarter is expected to average 4.9 percent, down from 6.1 percent in the previous Reuters poll.
All economists polled said they had cut their forecasts as a result of the slump in demand for electronics and related components, on which Singapore is heavily dependent.
Electronics and related products account for about half the city-state's industrial production and almost 60 percent of its non-oil exports.
And most economists said they might consider revising their forecasts further if Singapore latest trade data for September, due to be published on Monday, are worse than expected.

A Reuters poll of economists on Thursday predicted the Trade Development Board would report a fall of 3.4 percent in the city-state's non-oil exports for September, compared with a fall of 6.3 percent in August.
